text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act (good cause eviction)","requirement":"A landlord may recover possession of a residential unit only by tenant consent or through court eviction, and must have statutory good cause to evict or to fail to renew a lease, written or oral. Each cause except nonpayment of rent must be described in detail in a written notice. A Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment of rent. Some causes also require a prior written Notice to Cease. Notice to Quit periods: 3 days (disorderly conduct, property damage, employment-based tenancy, drug offense, assault or threats against landlord); 1 month (breach of rules or covenants, rent increase nonpayment, lease changes, habitual late payment); 3 months (health and safety violations or removal from the rental market, where relocation assistance is required first); 18 months (permanently retiring the property from residential use); 3 years (condominium, cooperative or fee simple conversion); 2 months (owner occupancy or sale to an owner-occupant). Only a court officer may carry out an eviction, after a judgment and warrant. Self-help evictions and lockouts are illegal. For a tenant evicted because of an illegal occupancy (ground G(3)), the landlord must pay relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent.
